analogies: A junior analyst who never leaves the office — you assign the work, and they come to you with results.
definition: Dots are OpenAI's always-on AI agents, announced at DevDay 2026. Unlike a chatbot that answers and stops, a dot keeps working toward a goal after you close the chat. Each dot gets its own cloud computer — a rented machine that runs online rather than on your device — plus its own browser, and it can connect to more than 4,000 apps. It works in the background, learns from your feedback over time, and checks back in when there's something to report. Dots are powered by OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model, and you message them inside ChatGPT, Slack, or Teams.

example.body: On Monday morning you tell your dot: “Watch the sales numbers and have a summary ready by Friday.” You never open the chat again. Tuesday it spots the numbers in your connected spreadsheet app. Wednesday it pulls context from two internal docs. Thursday it flags that one region's figures look wrong and double-checks. Friday morning the summary is waiting — with a note about the odd figures. You message it from Slack to steer it, and it keeps going.
example.title: The Friday report

footnotes.body: Announced in the DevDay 2026 keynote, September 29, 2026, at Fort Mason, San Francisco. At launch, Dots were available on ChatGPT Pro 200 and Business Premium, with admin-approved beta access for Enterprise, Education, and Healthcare plans — off by default. Not on Free, Plus, or standard Pro initially. Texting support was described as “coming soon.” Availability and pricing will change; treat these details as a snapshot.

name: Dots
tagline: Always-on AI agents that keep working on your goals in the background, even after you close the chat.
whyItMatters: This is the biggest shift yet in what a chatbot is: from something you talk to, to something you delegate to. Dots make the “agentic” promise concrete — an assistant that works while you're in a meeting. They also concentrate trust: a background agent with access to thousands of your apps is powerful precisely where governance matters most.
